---
title: "Song / non-song glutamatergic pairing by dataset integration (hybrid labels)"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    df-print: paged
---

A complementary test of the song / non-song cell-type pairings, independent of the
hierarchical clustering in `snrna/trees/celltypes_hclust_glut_robustness_hybrid.qmd`.

The clustering approach controls for song-nucleus identity by *removing song DEGs* before
building the tree, and the reviewer's concern is that the pairings might be an artifact of
that removal step. Integration controls for the same axis a completely different way: the
song and non-song glutamatergic neurons are treated as two **datasets**, the
dataset-level difference is removed by anchor-based integration, and we then ask which
non-song cell type each song cell type aligns to. No gene is removed at any point, and no
tree is built, so the two methods fail differently.

Two readouts come out of one anchor computation per parameter set:

1. **Anchor partners.** `FindIntegrationAnchors()` pairs individual song cells with
   individual non-song cells. Tabulating the non-song cell type of each song cell's anchor
   partners is the most direct possible statement of "which type does this song type pair
   with" -- it is the integration's own correspondence, before any correction is applied.
2. **Co-embedding neighbours.** `IntegrateData()` on the same anchors, then, in the
   corrected space, the nearest non-song neighbours of every song cell. This is the
   "which types do the song neurons integrate with" question asked after the correction
   rather than before it.

Each dataset is normalised with **SCTransform** and integrated with
`normalization.method = "SCT"`, matching the normalisation used throughout this project.
The object's existing SCT assay is deliberately not reused: it was fit across all cells at
once, so it already absorbs the very song/non-song difference the integration is meant to
estimate.

Both are swept over **integration strength** (`k.anchor`) and over **RPCA vs CCA**, per the
reviewer's suggestion. `k.anchor` sets how many neighbours count as a mutual-nearest-neighbour
anchor: small values give few, high-confidence anchors, large values force more of the two
datasets into correspondence. A pairing that survives from `k.anchor = 5` to `k.anchor = 50`
under both reductions is not an artifact of the integration strength.

**Counting caveat, handled throughout.** Anchors and neighbours both scale with cell-type
size: a non-song type with 1800 cells will collect more anchors than one with 200 for no
biological reason. Every panel therefore reports a size-normalised enrichment,
`log2(observed / expected)`, alongside the raw share, where expected is the share that type
would get if partners were assigned in proportion to cell number.

```{r setup}
#| message: false
library(Seurat)
library(tidyverse)
library(qs2)
library(Matrix)
library(RANN)
library(cowplot)
library(here)
set.seed(10)

## Arial is not a font the base pdf() device knows; render chunk figures through
## ragg, and let fig_save() handle the vector output via cairo_pdf.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 200)

source(here::here("config/figure_theme.R"))
source(file.path(Sys.getenv("COLQUITTLAB_UTILS", "/opt/colquittlab/utils"), "R", "common_aesthetics.R"))

options(future.globals.maxSize = Inf)
```

# Parameters

```{r params}
label_col   = "celltype_hybrid"   # cluster labels (hybrid division naming)
assay_raw   = "RNA"               # counts to renormalise per dataset
norm_method = "SCT"               # per-dataset normalisation for the integration
n_features  = 3000                # SelectIntegrationFeatures (SCT convention here)
dims_to_use = 1:30
n_knn       = 20                  # neighbours per song cell in the corrected space

## Integration strength sweep, per the reviewer's suggestion
k_anchors   = c(5, 10, 20, 30, 50)
reductions  = c("rpca", "cca")
## The value to use where a single setting has to be named in the text/figures
k_ref       = 5

## Song-nucleus cell types under the hybrid labels. Everything else glutamatergic
## is the non-song set.
song_pattern = "HVC|LMAN|-RA$"

## Analyses: the two excitatory divisions separately (which is the comparison the
## manuscript makes -- a song nucleus against its own local surround), and both
## pooled.
set_defs = list(
  ARCO = "^Glut-CACNA1H-",
  NIDO = "^Glut-DACH2-",
  ALL  = "^Glut-"
)
sets = names(set_defs)

n_threads = min(16L, max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 4L))
RhpcBLASctl::blas_set_num_threads(n_threads)
RcppParallel::setThreadOptions(numThreads = n_threads)
```

# Directories

```{r dirs}
script_name = "song_nonsong_integration_hybrid"

## Read-only input: the glutamatergic subset already assembled by the clustering
## notebook (same cells, same exclusions), so the two analyses cannot drift apart
## on which cells they consider.
obj_fname = here::here("snrna/trees/celltypes_hclust_glut_robustness_hybrid",
                       "obj_clustered_glutamatergic.qs2")

## Hierarchical-clustering pairings, to compare against at the end
hclust_pairs_fname = here::here("snrna/trees/celltypes_hclust_glut_robustness_hybrid",
                                "correlation_ward.D", "song_pair_support.csv")

out_dir   = here::here("snrna/integration", script_name)
cache_dir = file.path(out_dir, "cache")
dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Load

```{r load}
obj = qs_read(obj_fname, nthreads = 8)

## The saved object carries the hybrid labels in `celltype_hybrid`; its `cluster`
## column is still the original naming (the clustering notebook overwrites that
## only after saving). Use the hybrid column explicitly.
obj$label = droplevels(as.factor(obj@meta.data[[label_col]]))
obj$is_song = grepl(song_pattern, obj$label)
obj$set = ifelse(obj$is_song, "song", "nonsong")

song_types    = sort(unique(as.character(obj$label[obj$is_song])))
nonsong_types = sort(unique(as.character(obj$label[!obj$is_song])))

tibble(set = c("song", "non-song"),
       n_types = c(length(song_types), length(nonsong_types)),
       n_cells = c(sum(obj$is_song), sum(!obj$is_song)),
       types = c(paste(song_types, collapse = ", "),
                 paste(nonsong_types, collapse = ", ")))
```

```{r load-check}
## Every song type is one nucleus's own cluster, but the NON-song set draws cells
## from all six dissections, including the song-nucleus libraries (surround tissue
## captured in the same dissection). That matters: if the non-song set came only
## from the surround dissections, "song vs non-song" would be perfectly confounded
## with library and the integration would be removing a pure batch effect.
table(obj$set, obj$sample_name)
```

# Integration sweep

One `FindIntegrationAnchors()` per (analysis set x reduction x `k.anchor`), with
`IntegrateData()` run from the same anchors so both readouts describe the same
integration. Cached per parameter set.

```{r sweep-fns}
## Split into the two datasets and renormalise each on its own, which is what makes
## them independent datasets rather than one dataset with a label. SCT per dataset,
## following the same idiom as the other integrations in this directory
## (snrna/integration/cca_glut_sweep/prep.R): SCTransform each, pick integration
## features across both, PrepSCTIntegration, then a per-object PCA on those
## features for RPCA to project into.
##
## The object's existing SCT assay is NOT reused: it was fit on all the cells at
## once, so it already carries the song/non-song difference the integration is
## supposed to be estimating. Each dataset has to be modelled on its own.
prep_pair = function(obj_set) {
  ## The RNA assay on this object is BPCells-backed on disk, and Seurat's VST path
  ## for an IterableMatrix fails on a subset this size. Materialise the counts and
  ## rebuild a plain object carrying just what the integration needs.
  cnt = as(LayerData(obj_set, assay = assay_raw, layer = "counts"), "dgCMatrix")
  keep_md = c("set", "label", "sample_name", "position")
  mem = CreateSeuratObject(cnt, meta.data = obj_set@meta.data[, keep_md, drop = FALSE])
  lst = SplitObject(mem, split.by = "set")
  lst = lst[c("song", "nonsong")]

  lst = lapply(lst, function(x) SCTransform(x, verbose = FALSE))
  features = SelectIntegrationFeatures(lst, nfeatures = n_features, verbose = FALSE)
  lst = PrepSCTIntegration(lst, anchor.features = features, verbose = FALSE)
  lst = lapply(lst, function(x)
    RunPCA(x, features = features, npcs = max(dims_to_use), verbose = FALSE))
  list(list = lst, features = features)
}

## SCTransform is the expensive step and depends only on the analysis set, not on
## the reduction or k.anchor, so fit it once per set and reuse it across that
## set's ten parameter combinations. One slot: the sweep is ordered set-major, so
## a single-entry memo is enough and never holds two large objects at once.
prep_slot = list(name = NULL, value = NULL)
get_prep = function(set_name) {
  if (identical(prep_slot$name, set_name)) return(prep_slot$value)
  f = file.path(cache_dir, sprintf("prep_%s.qs2", set_name))
  if (file.exists(f)) {
    p = qs_read(f, nthreads = 8)
  } else {
    message("== SCTransform: ", set_name)
    cells = colnames(obj)[grepl(set_defs[[set_name]], obj$label)]
    obj_set = subset(obj, cells = cells)
    obj_set$label = droplevels(obj_set$label)
    p = prep_pair(obj_set)
    p$labels = setNames(as.character(obj_set$label), colnames(obj_set))
    ## dissection library per cell, for the within-library permutation null
    p$libs = setNames(as.character(obj_set$sample_name), colnames(obj_set))
    qs_save(p, f, nthreads = 8)
    rm(obj_set); gc()
  }
  prep_slot <<- list(name = set_name, value = p)
  p
}

## Anchor pairs as (song cell, non-song cell). FindIntegrationAnchors reports each
## pair from both directions; normalise so cell1 is always the song cell.
anchor_pairs = function(anchorset) {
  a = anchorset@anchors
  cells1 = Cells(anchorset@object.list[[1]])   # song   (list order is fixed above)
  cells2 = Cells(anchorset@object.list[[2]])   # nonsong
  fwd = a %>% filter(dataset1 == 1, dataset2 == 2) %>%
    transmute(song_cell = cells1[cell1], nonsong_cell = cells2[cell2], score)
  rev = a %>% filter(dataset1 == 2, dataset2 == 1) %>%
    transmute(song_cell = cells1[cell2], nonsong_cell = cells2[cell1], score)
  bind_rows(fwd, rev) %>% distinct(song_cell, nonsong_cell, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

## Shared summary: counts of song type x non-song type, with the size-normalised
## enrichment. `expected` is the share the non-song type would take if partners
## were drawn in proportion to how many cells it has.
partner_summary = function(song_lab, nonsong_lab, nonsong_sizes) {
  exp_share = nonsong_sizes / sum(nonsong_sizes)
  tibble(song_type = song_lab, nonsong_type = nonsong_lab) %>%
    count(song_type, nonsong_type, name = "n") %>%
    complete(song_type, nonsong_type = names(nonsong_sizes), fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
    group_by(song_type) %>%
    mutate(share = n / sum(n),
           expected = exp_share[nonsong_type],
           enrichment = log2((share + 1e-6) / (expected + 1e-6))) %>%
    ungroup()
}

run_one = function(set_name, reduction, k_anchor) {
  key = sprintf("%s_%s_k%02d", set_name, reduction, k_anchor)
  f   = file.path(cache_dir, paste0(key, ".qs2"))
  if (file.exists(f)) return(qs_read(f))
  message("== ", key)

  prep = get_prep(set_name)

  anchors = FindIntegrationAnchors(prep$list, anchor.features = prep$features,
                                   normalization.method = norm_method,
                                   reduction = reduction, dims = dims_to_use,
                                   k.anchor = k_anchor, verbose = FALSE)

  lab = prep$labels
  nonsong_sizes = table(lab[!grepl(song_pattern, lab)])
  nonsong_sizes = setNames(as.numeric(nonsong_sizes), names(nonsong_sizes))

  ## --- readout 1: anchor partners -----------------------------------------
  ap = anchor_pairs(anchors)
  ## The anchor table indexes into object.list by position, so a wrong list order
  ## or index base would silently produce a plausible-looking but meaningless
  ## table. Assert the mapping instead of trusting it.
  stopifnot(all(grepl(song_pattern, lab[ap$song_cell])),
            !any(grepl(song_pattern, lab[ap$nonsong_cell])))
  anchor_tab = partner_summary(lab[ap$song_cell], lab[ap$nonsong_cell], nonsong_sizes) %>%
    mutate(readout = "anchor")

  ## --- readout 2: neighbours in the corrected space ------------------------
  k_weight = min(100, min(vapply(prep$list, ncol, integer(1))) - 1)
  int = IntegrateData(anchorset = anchors, normalization.method = norm_method,
                      dims = dims_to_use, k.weight = k_weight, verbose = FALSE)
  DefaultAssay(int) = "integrated"
  ## No ScaleData here: IntegrateData(normalization.method = "SCT") returns the
  ## integrated assay already scaled, and re-scaling would undo it.
  int = RunPCA(int, npcs = max(dims_to_use), verbose = FALSE)
  emb = Embeddings(int, "pca")[, dims_to_use]

  is_song_cell  = grepl(song_pattern, lab[colnames(int)])
  song_cells    = colnames(int)[is_song_cell]
  nonsong_cells = colnames(int)[!is_song_cell]
  nn = RANN::nn2(emb[nonsong_cells, , drop = FALSE],
                 emb[song_cells, , drop = FALSE],
                 k = min(n_knn, length(nonsong_cells)))
  nb = tibble(song_cell = rep(song_cells, times = ncol(nn$nn.idx)),
              nonsong_cell = nonsong_cells[as.vector(nn$nn.idx)])
  nn_tab = partner_summary(lab[nb$song_cell], lab[nb$nonsong_cell], nonsong_sizes) %>%
    mutate(readout = "neighbour")

  ## How far the two datasets actually merged: of each song cell's n_knn nearest
  ## cells overall, the fraction that are non-song. 0 = still separate,
  ## ~(non-song share of cells) = fully mixed.
  nn_all = RANN::nn2(emb, emb[song_cells, , drop = FALSE], k = n_knn + 1)
  all_cells = rownames(emb)
  frac_cross = mean(all_cells[as.vector(nn_all$nn.idx[, -1])] %in% nonsong_cells)

  ## The pair lists are kept, not just their summary: a label-shuffling null has
  ## to permute labels on this exact graph, and it cannot be reconstructed from
  ## the counts.
  res = list(set = set_name, reduction = reduction, k_anchor = k_anchor,
             pairs_anchor = ap,
             pairs_neighbour = nb,
             cell_meta = tibble(cell = names(prep$labels),
                                label = unname(prep$labels),
                                library = unname(prep$libs[names(prep$labels)])),
             n_anchors = nrow(ap),
             frac_cross_neighbours = frac_cross,
             mixing_expected = length(nonsong_cells) / nrow(emb),
             table = bind_rows(anchor_tab, nn_tab) %>%
               mutate(set = set_name, reduction = reduction, k_anchor = k_anchor))
  qs_save(res, f, nthreads = 4)
  rm(int, anchors); gc()
  res
}
```

```{r sweep}
#| message: false
grid = expand_grid(set = sets, reduction = reductions, k_anchor = k_anchors)
runs = pmap(grid, function(set, reduction, k_anchor) run_one(set, reduction, k_anchor))

## Enrichment is recomputed here rather than taken from the cached tables, with
## add-one smoothing. A partner type that collects zero anchors would otherwise
## take log2 of a bare pseudocount and land near -15, which swamps the diverging
## colour scale and hides the differences among the types that actually do pair.
## Smoothing bounds the empty cells without touching the ordering of the rest.
partners = map_dfr(runs, "table") %>%
  group_by(readout, set, reduction, k_anchor, song_type) %>%
  mutate(share_smoothed = (n + 1) / (sum(n) + n()),
         enrichment = log2(share_smoothed / expected)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(k_anchor = factor(k_anchor, levels = k_anchors),
         set = factor(set, levels = sets))
write_csv(partners, file.path(out_dir, "partner_composition.csv"))

run_info = map_dfr(runs, function(r)
  tibble(set = r$set, reduction = r$reduction, k_anchor = r$k_anchor,
         n_anchors = r$n_anchors,
         frac_cross_neighbours = r$frac_cross_neighbours,
         mixing_expected = r$mixing_expected))
write_csv(run_info, file.path(out_dir, "run_summary.csv"))
run_info
```

# Which non-song type does each song type pair with?

```{r top-partner}
## Two ways to call the partner, reported side by side because they can disagree
## when cell-type sizes are very unequal: the size-normalised enrichment (primary,
## since a big non-song type collects partners for free) and the raw share of
## partners (what the integration literally did, uncorrected).
top_partner = partners %>%
  group_by(readout, set, reduction, k_anchor, song_type) %>%
  summarise(top_partner       = nonsong_type[which.max(enrichment)],
            enrichment        = max(enrichment),
            share             = share[which.max(enrichment)],
            top_partner_share = nonsong_type[which.max(share)],
            share_of_top      = max(share),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(criteria_agree = top_partner == top_partner_share)
write_csv(top_partner, file.path(out_dir, "top_partner.csv"))

## Does the top partner hold across the whole k.anchor sweep?
consistency = top_partner %>%
  group_by(readout, set, reduction, song_type) %>%
  summarise(n_k = n(), n_distinct_partners = n_distinct(top_partner),
            modal_partner = names(sort(table(top_partner), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
            frac_k_at_modal = mean(top_partner == modal_partner),
            modal_partner_by_share = names(sort(table(top_partner_share), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
            frac_criteria_agree = mean(criteria_agree),
            .groups = "drop")
write_csv(consistency, file.path(out_dir, "top_partner_consistency.csv"))
consistency
```

# Figures

```{r fig-fns}
## Strip the shared prefix so labels fit at 5 pt. The division prefix is constant
## within the ARCO and NIDO panels and only tells anything apart in ALL, so it is
## abbreviated rather than dropped.
short = function(x) {
  x %>%
    str_replace("^Glut-DACH2-", "D2-") %>%
    str_replace("^Glut-CACNA1H-", "C1H-") %>%
    str_replace("^Glut-", "")
}

song_position = function(x) case_when(grepl("LMAN", x) ~ "lman",
                                      grepl("HVC", x)  ~ "hvc",
                                      grepl("RA", x)   ~ "ra",
                                      TRUE             ~ NA_character_)

## Row order and colour, matching the clustering figures: grouped by nucleus,
## labels in the standard HVC / LMAN / RA position colours.
song_levels = function(x) {
  u = unique(as.character(x))
  rev(u[order(match(song_position(u), c("hvc", "lman", "ra")), u)])
}
```

```{r fig-enrichment}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
## Full composition: song type x non-song type, one column block per k.anchor.
enrich_plot = function(d, ttl) {
  lv = song_levels(d$song_type)
  d = d %>% mutate(song_type = factor(as.character(song_type), levels = lv))
  axis_cols = unname(position_colors[song_position(lv)])
  ## clip at the strongest positive signal: depletion is not the point here, and
  ## letting it set the limits flattens everything else
  lim = max(abs(d$enrichment), na.rm = TRUE)
  lim = min(lim, max(3, ceiling(max(d$enrichment, na.rm = TRUE))))
  ggplot(d, aes(short(nonsong_type), song_type, fill = enrichment)) +
    geom_tile(colour = FIG_SURFACE, linewidth = 0.2) +
    facet_grid(reduction ~ k_anchor, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x",
               labeller = labeller(k_anchor = function(x) paste0("k.anchor ", x))) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = FIG_DIV_LOW, mid = FIG_DIV_MID, high = FIG_DIV_HIGH,
                         midpoint = 0, limits = c(-lim, lim),
                         oob = scales::squish, name = "log2 obs/exp") +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = fig_expand()) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = short, expand = fig_expand()) +
    labs(x = "non-song cell type", y = NULL, title = ttl) +
    theme_fig() +
    ## theme_fig() sets panel.grid.major explicitly, and a specific element
    ## beats the panel.grid parent, so both children have to be blanked
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),
          axis.text.y = element_text(colour = axis_cols),
          panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(size = FIG_PT_AXIS_TITLE,
                                    colour = FIG_INK_SECONDARY))
}

for (rd in c("anchor", "neighbour")) {
  for (st in sets) {
    d = filter(partners, readout == rd, set == st)
    if (!nrow(d)) next
    p = enrich_plot(d, sprintf("%s | %s partners", st, rd))
    print(p)
    fig_save(p, file.path(out_dir, sprintf("enrichment_%s_%s", rd, tolower(st))),
             width = 1.2 + 0.11 * length(unique(d$nonsong_type)) * length(k_anchors),
             height = 2.4)
  }
}
```

```{r fig-top-partner}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3
## The summary panel, in the same idiom as the clustering figure: rows = song
## types, columns = integration strength, tile text = the partner it pairs with,
## fill = how enriched that pairing is.
top_plot = function(d, ttl) {
  lv = song_levels(d$song_type)
  d = d %>% mutate(song_type = factor(as.character(song_type), levels = lv),
                   lab = short(top_partner))
  axis_cols = unname(position_colors[song_position(lv)])
  ggplot(d, aes(k_anchor, song_type, fill = enrichment)) +
    geom_tile(colour = FIG_SURFACE, linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = lab), size = fig_pt(5), family = FIG_FONT,
              colour = FIG_INK_PRIMARY) +
    facet_wrap(~reduction, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = FIG_SURFACE, high = FIG_PAL[1],
                        name = "log2 obs/exp") +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = fig_expand()) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = short, expand = fig_expand()) +
    labs(x = "k.anchor (integration strength)", y = NULL, title = ttl) +
    theme_fig() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(colour = axis_cols),
          panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(size = FIG_PT_AXIS_TITLE,
                                    colour = FIG_INK_SECONDARY))
}

for (rd in c("anchor", "neighbour")) {
  for (st in sets) {
    d = filter(top_partner, readout == rd, set == st)
    if (!nrow(d)) next
    p = top_plot(d, sprintf("%s | top %s partner", st, rd))
    print(p)
    fig_save(p, file.path(out_dir, sprintf("top_partner_%s_%s", rd, tolower(st))),
             width = 1.4 + 0.34 * length(k_anchors) * length(reductions),
             height = 0.32 * n_distinct(d$song_type) + 1.0)
  }
}
```

```{r fig-mixing}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 2
## Sanity check on the sweep itself: integration strength should actually change
## how much the two datasets merge, or the sweep is not testing anything.
p_mix = run_info %>%
  mutate(k_anchor = factor(k_anchor, levels = k_anchors)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(k_anchor, frac_cross_neighbours, colour = reduction,
             group = interaction(reduction, set))) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = mixing_expected), linetype = 2,
             colour = FIG_INK_MUTED, linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.3) + geom_point(size = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~set, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = FIG_PAL[1:2]) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = fig_expand()) +
  labs(x = "k.anchor", y = "non-song fraction of\nsong cells' neighbours",
       caption = paste("dashed = the non-song share of all cells, i.e. the value if the two sets",
                       "were indistinguishable.\nStaying below it is expected -- song and non-song",
                       "are genuinely different cell types; integration\nremoves the dataset-level",
                       "offset, it does not merge distinct types.")) +
  theme_fig() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = FIG_PT_AXIS_TITLE, colour = FIG_INK_SECONDARY))
print(p_mix)
fig_save(p_mix, file.path(out_dir, "mixing_by_k"), width = 4.2, height = 1.6)
```

# Agreement with the hierarchical clustering

The two methods share no machinery: one removes song DEGs and builds a correlation tree on
pseudobulk profiles, the other keeps every gene and matches individual cells across two
datasets. Where they name the same partner, that pairing does not depend on either method's
particular control for song-nucleus identity.

```{r agreement}
hclust_pairs = read_csv(hclust_pairs_fname, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(region %in% c("ARCO", "NIDO"), threshold_label == "0.1") %>%
  transmute(set = region, song_type = song_cluster,
            hclust_partner = sister, hclust_au = au)

agreement = top_partner %>%
  filter(set %in% c("ARCO", "NIDO")) %>%
  left_join(hclust_pairs, by = c("set", "song_type")) %>%
  mutate(partner_in_hclust_set = map2_lgl(top_partner, hclust_partner,
                                          ~ !is.na(.y) && .x %in% str_split(.y, ",\\s*")[[1]]))
write_csv(agreement, file.path(out_dir, "agreement_with_hclust.csv"))

agreement %>%
  group_by(readout, reduction, song_type) %>%
  summarise(hclust_partner = first(hclust_partner),
            integration_partners = paste(sort(unique(top_partner)), collapse = ", "),
            frac_k_agreeing = mean(partner_in_hclust_set), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(readout, reduction, song_type)
```
